title: Local flat base change covered by closed-fibre associated primes is universally injective
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative local rings (each has exactly one maximal ideal), with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R$ and $\mathfrak m_S$, and let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism (it maps $\mathfrak m_R$ into $\mathfrak m_S$) which is essentially of finite presentation: $S$ is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to a localization $W^{-1}B$ of a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let $N$ be a finitely presented $S$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] which is flat as an $R$-module, and let $S\to S'$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose the image of $\operatorname{Spec}S'\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains every prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak m_R$ and which is an element-annihilator associated prime of the $S$-module $N/\mathfrak m_RN$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Then the canonical $R$-linear map $u:N\to N\otimes_SS'$, $n\mapsto n\otimes1$, is universally injective over $R$: for every $R$-module $L$, the map $u\otimes_R1_L:N\otimes_RL\to(N\otimes_SS')\otimes_RL$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: Write $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, $C=S/\mathfrak m_RS$, and $\overline N=N/\mathfrak m_RN$. From the given presentation $S=W^{-1}B$, reduction of coefficients and fractions gives $C\cong\overline W^{-1}(B/\mathfrak m_RB)$: the map sends the class of $b/w$ to $\bar b/\bar w$, and its inverse uses the same lifts, since changing a lift by an element of $\mathfrak m_RB$ changes the fraction by zero modulo $\mathfrak m_RS$. The ring $B/\mathfrak m_RB$ is a quotient of $k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ by the reductions of the finitely many defining relations, hence is of finite type over $k$. A field is Noetherian because its ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal, generated by $0$ and $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to conclude that $C$ is Noetherian. A finite generating set from the finite presentation of $N$ maps to generators of $\overline N$ over $C$. Thus all closed-fibre hypotheses of 05DE are verified without assuming $S$ or $R$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05DG (lemma-base-change-universally-flat-local), application of 05DE; finite-presentation hypotheses expanded.

proof.text: Let $\Sigma$ consist of the scalars acting injectively on $\overline N$, and put $T=\Sigma^{-1}S$, $T'=\Sigma^{-1}S'$, using the image of $\Sigma$ for the latter localization. By [lem-sfb-fibre-regular-localization-spectrum], $\Sigma$ is multiplicative and every maximal ideal $P$ of $T$ contracts to an associated prime $\mathfrak q$ of $\overline N$ in $S$, disjoint from $\Sigma$. Every $r\in\mathfrak m_R$ kills $\overline N$, so belongs to each element annihilator; consequently $\mathfrak q\cap R$ contains $\mathfrak m_R$, and equals it because it is proper. The coverage hypothesis supplies a prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $S'$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$. It misses the image of $\Sigma$, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] supplies a prime $P'$ of $T'$ over $\mathfrak q'$. Its contraction to $T$ is $P$: for $a\in S$, $s\in\Sigma$, membership of $a/s$ in either contracted prime is precisely $a\in\mathfrak q$, since denominators are units. In particular $PT'\subseteq P'$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 05DG, middle paragraph, using 05DE and localization of primes.

proof.text: The ring $T'$ is the base change $T\otimes_S S'$: the mutually inverse maps are $(a/s)\otimes b\mapsto ab/s$ and $b/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes b$. The fraction relation makes both well-defined, and the composites are identities on fractions and on pure tensors, which generate. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] to the flat $S$-module $S'$ and $S\to T$ to see that $T'$ is flat over $T$. Step 2 showed $PT'\ne T'$ for every maximal ideal $P$ of $T$, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] makes $T\to T'$ faithfully flat. This argument includes $T=0$, when $T'=0$ and the maximal-ideal condition is empty.

source.place: Tag 05DG, middle paragraph, faithful flatness via algebra.tex Tags 00HI and 00HP (equivalently 00HQ).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibre-regular-localization-universal-injection] to the original local map $R\to S$ and module $N$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given essential finite presentation, finite presentation of $N$, and $R$-flatness. With the same $\Sigma$, it gives injectivity of $N\otimes_R L\to(\Sigma^{-1}N)\otimes_R L$ for every $R$-module $L$.

Fix any $R$-module $L$, and put $X=(\Sigma^{-1}N)\otimes_R L$, a $T$-module by the action on its first factor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to the faithfully flat map $T\to T'$ from step 3 and to this arbitrary $T$-module $X$. It gives an injection $X\to X\otimes_T T'$. Put $N'=N\otimes_S S'$. The explicit isomorphism $X\otimes_T T'\cong(\Sigma^{-1}N')\otimes_R L$ sends $((n/s)\otimes l)\otimes(b/t)$ to $((n\otimes b)/(st))\otimes l$; its inverse sends $((n\otimes b)/s)\otimes l$ to $((n/s)\otimes l)\otimes(b/1)$. Bilinearity, the balancing relations and the fraction equality relation show these are well-defined inverse maps (check the composites on the displayed generators). Under them the injection sends $(n/s)\otimes l$ to $((n\otimes1)/s)\otimes l$. Thus it is precisely the localized scalar-extension map tensored over $R$ with $L$.

source.place: Tag 05DG, middle-to-final paragraphs, using algebra.tex Tag 05CK; tensor identifications written on generators.

proof.text: Compose the injections of steps 4 and 5. The composite sends $n\otimes l$ to $((n\otimes1)/1)\otimes l$. It factors as $u\otimes_R1_L$ followed by localization on $N'\otimes_R L$, since both maps have that same formula on pure tensors. If $(u\otimes_R1_L)(z)=0$, this injective composite kills $z$, so $z=0$. Since $L$ was arbitrary, $u$ is universally injective over $R$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q70-593dbe93b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks flat.tex 05DE, 05DF and 05DG with their proofs. The item's hypotheses (1)-(6) and its conclusion match 05DG exactly; the statement is not weakened. Two corrections in the delivery are right. First, the source proof writes N⊗_R S′ where N⊗_S S′ is meant; this is a typo confined to the proof, confirmed on R=k, S=S′=k[x]_(x), N=S. Second, the sheaf finite-presentation definition was replaced by def-sc-finitely-presented-module (Tag 0518), the notion for ring modules. Step 1: the closed fibre C ≅ W̄⁻¹(B/m_R B) is Noetherian by 00FN (finite type over a field, then localization), and N̄ is finite over C. Step 2: by the 05DE node, maximal ideals of T contract to maximal associated primes, and these lie over m_R. The coverage hypothesis gives q′ in S′, 00E3 gives P′ in T′, and P′ contracts to P, so PT′ is proper. Step 3: T′≅T⊗_S S′ by explicit inverse maps; 00HI makes it flat over T and 00HP makes T→T′ faithfully flat. Step 4: the new 05DF node, whose hypotheses match. Step 5: 05CK applied to X=Σ⁻¹N⊗_R L, with X⊗_T T′≅Σ⁻¹N′⊗_R L written out on generators. Step 6: injectivity of the composite gives injectivity of u⊗1, which is elementary. The new node lem-sfb-fibre-regular-localization-universal-injection is a statement only and equivalent to 05DF: the 05DE assumptions it omits follow from its finite presentation hypotheses. I tested it on N=0, on a field, on a unit scalar, and on R=k, S=k[x]_(x). It is strictly smaller than the item and does not restate the parent 05DH. An rg -L search for 05DF and universal injectivity found no duplicate; the nearest nodes are 046Y, 05FQ and 05CM. There is no cycle, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and there is no SGA citation. The tool_uses are generic commutative-algebra Mathlib-leaf nodes and are accepted. The live node is still unsplit and has no repair note. One remark only: the report mentions citations.json and searches.jsonl files that are not in the commit.
